title: Director, AI Governance & Risk
description: JOB SUMMARY: The Office of General Counsel is responsible for overseeing all elements of the Firm's privacy compliance program. This program includes the Firm's privacy policies, notices, records of processing, impact assessments, transfer agreements, data processing agreements, data subject access requests and all other matters related to complying with applicable privacy and data security laws. The Director, AI Governance & Risk will play a key role in maturing, implementing, and overseeing Simpson Thacher’s AI governance framework, policies and controls to ensure responsible, ethical, secure and compliant use of artificial intelligence. This role will report to the Chief Risk Officer and will be part of a multi-disciplinary team focused on accelerating the adoption of appropriate AI tools and technologies across the Firm. The Director will bridge legal, risk, compliance, technology & business teams to manage AI-related risks across the full AI lifecycle – from ideation and development to deployment and monitoring. As a senior leader , t he Director will lead Firm-wide AI governance initiatives, align AI practices with regulatory requirements and industry standards, and serve as a key advisor to Partners and Senior Leadership on AI risk, ethics and controls. JOB DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES: Develop, implement and maintain the Firm’s AI governance framework, including policies, standards, controls and operation procedures Establish governance processes for evaluating AI use cases, the selection of appropriate tools and technologies, assessing technology developments and vendor due diligence Ensure data and information governance aligns, enables and supports the adoption of AI tools and technologies Support the development and enhancement of AI user capability across the Firm, including the development of appropriate training for lawyers, professional staff and leaders Identify, assess and mitigate AI-related risks, including data privacy, cybersecurity, and third party/vendor risk Partner with the Office of General Counsel, Information Security, Information Governance and Knowledge & Innovation teams to integrate AI risks in existing risk frameworks Monitor and interpret global AI-related regulation standards and ensure AI systems and practices comply with applicable laws, regulations and internal policies Advise the Firm in relation to responsible AI principles and ethical guidelines Serve as a trusted advisor to Partners and Senior Leadership on AI risk and governance matters Drive AI governance awareness and training across the Firm Promote a culture of responsible AI use and accountability EDUCATION: JD required SKILLS & EXPERIENCE: Qualified lawyer, with 6-10 years of practicing experience at an international law firm Minimum 2-5 years of relevant experience in AI, risk and compliance Strategic thinking with strong execution capability Regulatory interpretation and policy development Demonstrated experience supporting and executing large-scale, firm-wide projects Cross-functional leadership and excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to influence the actions of internal stakeholders and manage relationships with external stakeholders Broad knowledge of information management and protection laws, regulations, and best practices Ability to balance innovation with risk management POSTING DISCLOSURE: Simpson Thacher will not sponsor applicants for work visas for this position. Salary Information NY Only: The estimated base salary range for this position is $325,000 to $375,000 at the time of posting. The actual salary offered will depend on a variety of factors, including without limitation, the qualifications of the individual applicant for the position, years of relevant experience, level of education attained, certifications or other professional licenses held, and if applicable, the location in which the applicant lives and/or from which they will be performing the job. This role is exempt meaning it is not overtime pay eligible. Simpson Thacher will not sponsor applicants for work visas for this position. title: Operational Risk Manager
description: Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states. We are looking for a systems-minded Operational Risk Manager to mature and scale our day-to-day risk and safety infrastructure. This isn't about running periodic checklists; it’s about turning operational data and playbooks into a live, predictive engine that actively shapes our product roadmap. In this role, you’ll embed directly with cross-functional teams to build the operational standards that allow us to scale safely and seamlessly. This role follows a hybrid work schedule and reports to the Head of Operations Safety & Readiness. You will: Mature & Publish Playbooks: Review, refine, and publish operational playbooks, ensuring they remain the accurate, optimized "source of truth." Day-to-Day Risk Management: Oversee continuous monitoring of operational risks, lead root cause investigations, and ensure compliance with our Safety Management System (SMS) and risk frameworks. Risk Register Ownership: Maintain, update, and govern the operational risk register, ensuring all tracked risks have clear owners, mitigation strategies, and regular status updates. Product Liaison: Translate day-to-day operational risk data, predictive analysis, and trends into nuanced requirements that secure roadmap prioritization from Product teams. Systems-Based Thinking: You analyze how our daily workflows interact, identifying bottlenecks or weak points in current frameworks to optimize the entire ecosystem. You have: Experience: 5+ years of Operational experience, with a focus on managing or maturing risk/operational workflows. Education: Bachelor's Degree in a relevant field or equivalent practical experience.  Tools & Framework Tracking: Direct experience with Jira and structured requirements tracking to manage operational priorities, action items, and cross-functional deliverables. Safety Framework Knowledge: Practical working knowledge of Safety Management Systems (SMS) principles and their application in fast-paced, live operational environments. Process Improvement & Systems Thinking: Proven track record of evaluating complex workflows, identifying failure modes, and authoring clear, comprehensive operational documentation. Communication & Collaboration: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to build trust, align diverse stakeholders, and influence without formal authority. We prefer: Prior experience in the Autonomous Vehicle (AV) industry. Operational risk or safety assurance experience within high-reliability and safety-critical industries (e.g., commercial aviation, defense, aerospace, rail/transit, energy, or complex fleet logistics). Experience with root-cause analysis methodologies (e.g., 5-Whys, Fishbone/Ishikawa, FMEA) and developing predictive operational indicators. Travel requirements: 20% The expected base salary range for this full-time position across US locations is listed below. Actual starting pay will be based on job-related factors, including exact work location, experience, relevant training and education, and skill level. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for the role location or, if the role can be performed remote, the specific salary range for your preferred location, during the hiring process.  Waymo employees are also eligible to participate in Waymo’s discretionary annual bonus program, equity incentive plan, and generous Company benefits program, subject to eligibility requirements.  Salary Range $159,000 — $196,000 USD

title: Business Control Manager
description: About the role We are hiring a Business Control Manager to join Chime’s Compliance Business Control Management team, with a primary focus on control delivery for Growth Marketing and Chime Enterprise. You will partner with business and control owners to translate agreed risk outcomes into practical controls that provide the right level of risk mitigation while working effectively for the business. You will also help bring Chime’s broader enterprise control environment to light by identifying, validating, and documenting controls that are already operating across the business. Along the way, you’ll have opportunities to contribute to larger Compliance BCM and business efforts based on priorities and capacity. In this role, you can expect to Partner with Growth Marketing and Chime Enterprise business and control owners to translate agreed risk and control outcomes into practical implementation plans, while supporting additional Compliance BCM portfolios based on priorities and capacity. Contribute to reviews of business requirements, projects, process or product changes, incidents, complaints, and regulatory developments by identifying relevant controls, operating practices, gaps, dependencies, and implementation considerations. Drive assigned control workstreams through implementation, validation, documentation, and closure, coordinating milestones, dependencies, evidence, and routine decisions with business and control owners. Evaluate Chime’s existing control environment by reviewing business activities, procedures, system capabilities, evidence, and current control records to identify controls already operating and potential coverage gaps. Assess whether existing controls provide appropriate coverage and recommend whether controls should be reused, enhanced, created, consolidated, or retired. Evaluate implementation readiness, coordinate control owner attestations, validate assigned controls against team standards, and maintain complete and current control records. Track gaps, exceptions, remediation commitments, and dependencies through closure, escalating material design, ownership, exposure, or delivery concerns and supporting remediation arising from incidents, testing, audits, or other findings. To thrive in this role, you have 4 or more years of experience in business controls, regulatory compliance, operational risk, audit, operations, or a related discipline within financial services, fintech, or another highly regulated environment. Hands-on experience taking a control or process improvement from a defined problem or requirement through implementation, evidence review, documentation, and closure. Strong analytical skills and experience evaluating business processes, requirements, incidents, and control records to understand what is operating, identify gaps, and determine where clarification or additional risk mitigation is needed. Strong execution and project-management skills, including managing multiple workstreams, dependencies, decisions, and stakeholders while adapting to changing complexity, urgency, and team priorities. Strong communication and influencing skills, with the ability to partner effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders, challenge incomplete evidence or unclear ownership, and escalate material concerns with sound judgment. Experience working in consumer financial services or another regulated environment, with working knowledge of regulatory and consumer protection risk frameworks such as EFTA and Regulation E, TILA and Regulation Z, UDAAP, or comparable requirements. #LI-Onsite #LI-LB1 Below is the base salary offered for this role and level of experience. Full-time employees may also be eligible for bonus(es), competitive equity, and benefits. For commissioned roles, the base salary listed in this job description does not include incentive/variable pay. The actual base salary offered may be higher, depending on your location, skills, qualifications, and experience. Wage Notice $101,000 — $140,000 USD A little about us At Chime, we believe that everyone can achieve financial progress. We created Chime—a financial technology company, not a bank*—on the premise that core banking services should be helpful, easy, and free. Through our user-friendly tools and intuitive platforms, we empower our members to take control of their finances and work towards their goals. Whether it's starting a savings account, purchasing a first car or home, launching a business, or pursuing higher education, we're proud to have helped millions unlock their financial potential. We're a team of problem solvers, dreamers, and builders with one shared obsession: our members. From day one, Chimers have worked tirelessly to out-hustle and out-execute competitors to bring our mission to life. title: Risk & Governance Manager
description: About the company Hi, we're Ondo Finance. Our mission is to provide institutional-grade, blockchain-enabled investment products and services. We have both a technology arm that develops decentralized finance technology, and an asset management arm that creates and manages tokenized funds. We were the first company to tokenize exposure to US Treasuries, and have since expanded into several other assets. We are also focused on incubating protocols that can support both tokenized real-world assets and traditional crypto.   Founded by folks from Goldman Sachs Digital Assets Team, we’re backed by some of the best investors in the world including Founders Fund, Coinbase Ventures, Pantera Capital, Tiger Global, and more. We are currently the leaders in the space in terms of AUM and are well capitalized to continue growing the firm. We're fully remote, with team members across the U.S. About the Role Ondo is looking to take its Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework, a structured Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) program, and a centralized policy library to the next level of maturity. As our product suite expands and the number of third-party relationships grows — spanning technology vendors, custodians, and distribution partners — we need a foundational team member who knows how to scale these workstreams in a meaningful regulatory, operational, and institutional way. We are looking for a Risk & Governance Manager to build upon the foundational risk and policy infrastructure. This role sits at the intersection of risk, policy, and audit readiness — three deeply interdependent areas are targeting dedicated ownership. Responsibilities Design and implement an Enterprise Risk Management framework, including a risk register, risk appetite statement, and reporting cadence for senior leadership and the board. Build and operate a Third Party Risk Management program covering all critical vendors — including vendor tiering, due diligence workflows, and ongoing monitoring against defined risk thresholds. Own and maintain the company's complete policy framework — including creation, review, approval, version control, and communication of all compliance and risk policies. Lead regulatory examination and institutional audit readiness, including documentation management, mock exam preparation, and response coordination. Provide governance support to senior leadership and the board, including risk reporting, escalation frameworks, and committee materials. Requirements 5+ years of experience in risk management, compliance, or governance within financial services or fintech Demonstrated experience building or managing an ERM framework, including risk registers and risk appetite statements Experience designing and operating Third-Party Risk Management programs, including vendor due diligence and ongoing monitoring Track record of owning and maintaining enterprise-wide policy libraries in a regulated environment Strong familiarity with regulatory examination processes and audit readiness requirements Exceptional written communication and documentation skills; able to produce board-ready materials Nice to Haves Experience in digital assets, blockchain, or crypto-native financial services Familiarity with governance frameworks such as COSO ERM, ISO 31000, or SOC 2 Background supporting institutional investors or regulated fund structures What we offer Competitive compensation including but not limited to salary, future token rights, and/or equity (according to your preferences) — We are well-funded and believe that great talent deserves great compensation. Full benefits (medical, vision, and dental) and flexible vacation policy (PTO). Remote-first team across many countries — You will be an early team member helping shape our vision, culture, and design practices. A+ colleagues — Our team includes alumni from: Goldman Sachs, Blackrock, Two Sigma, Bridgewater, SpaceX, AWS, Meta, Google, McKinsey, Circle, Uniswap. Best-in-class investors — We are proud to be backed by leading crypto experts and VCs, including Pantera Capital, Founders Fund and Coinbase Ventures.

title: Regulatory Delivery and Change Lead- Vice President
description: About this role The Regulatory Reporting Team: The Regulatory Reporting Team sits within BlackRock’s Reporting and Regulatory Solutions, part of Tech & Ops Business Operation Services. Regulatory Solutions is responsible for overseeing and delivering complex regulatory reporting obligations across trade and transaction reporting regulations, including MiFIR, EMIR, MAS, ASIC, SFTR, CSA, CFTC, NCCBR and 10c-1, alongside key reporting obligations across costs and charges, Solvency (TPT), and Sustainability domains including TCFD, SFDR and SDR. The team manages end-to-end reporting processes, partners with internal and external stakeholders, and drives strategic enhancements to data quality, control design and operational efficiency. We are looking for a Project Manager to help deliver regulatory reporting projects that protect clients, strengthen controls and support BlackRock’s regulatory commitments. This role will coordinate regulatory change initiatives, remediation activity and strategic platform enhancements that improve reporting compliance, accuracy, completeness, governance and operational resilience. Your role and impact: You will lead and support regulatory reporting projects that are critical to BlackRock’s compliance obligations and operational resilience. You will turn regulatory requirements into clear delivery plans, build trusted relationships across Operations, Compliance, Legal, Technology, Data, Product and external service providers, and help teams deliver sustainable outcomes with strong governance and controls. Your Responsibilities Lead and coordinate regulatory reporting projects across trade and transaction reporting regimes, costs and charges as well as Solvency and Sustainability. Design the correct structure of the project specific to each individual change Develop and maintain project plans, milestones, RAID logs, dependencies, governance materials and stakeholder communications. Work closely with Operations, Compliance, Legal, Technology, Data, Product and external providers to define scope, document requirements and support delivery against regulatory or internal deadlines. Support the design and implementation of scalable operating models, controls, reconciliations, exception management processes and data quality enhancements. Translate complex regulatory obligations into clear business, functional, data and technology requirements, with traceability from interpretation through implementation and testing. Support effective governance by preparing clear status updates, escalation materials and decision papers for senior stakeholders and regulatory reporting forums. Support testing, implementation readiness, post-implementation review and remediation activity so reporting processes remain robust, accurate and sustainable. Your Experience Experience in project management, regulatory change, business analysis or delivery within financial services, asset management, investment banking, consulting or another regulated environment. Experience delivering regulatory reporting or regulatory change projects; familiarity with the noted reporting regimes or related global reporting obligations would be helpful. Strong project delivery skills, including planning, governance, risk and issue management, dependency tracking, stakeholder engagement and implementation readiness. Ability to work with subject matter experts to interpret regulatory requirements and convert them into practical business, data, technology and control requirements. Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to make complex regulatory and technical topics understandable for different audiences. Experience collaborating with technology, operations, compliance, legal, data and vendor teams to deliver controlled, scalable and audit-ready outcomes. Knowledge of reporting controls, reconciliations, exception management, data lineage, testing and operational risk management is helpful but not required. Comfort working with data, workflow tools and project delivery platforms such as Aha, Python, PowerPoint or similar tools. Experience working with global teams across multiple cultures and time zones. Curiosity, attention to detail and a practical approach to raising risks, challenging assumptions and improving outcomes. Our benefits To help you stay energized, engaged and inspired, we offer a wide range of employee benefits including: retirement investment and tools designed to help you in building a sound financial future; access to education reimbursement; comprehensive resources to support your physical health and emotional well-being; family support programs; and Flexible Time Off (FTO) so you can relax, recharge and be there for the people you care about. Our hybrid work model BlackRock’s hybrid work model is designed to enable a culture of collaboration and apprenticeship that enriches the experience of our employees, while supporting flexibility for all.
